title: FAMPWQ: Fisher Information-based Adaptive Mixed Precision Weight Quantization for Effective LLM Inference
summary: Replaces uniform bit-width or heuristic-sensitivity weight quantization with layer-wise sensitivity measured by Fisher information and a reinforcement learning allocator that assigns per-layer bit-widths. Costs include a Fisher sensitivity estimation pass, training an RL allocator, and added deployment complexity from mixed-precision kernels, which may offset some memory savings relative to uniform low-bit formats. Can fail if Fisher estimates misrank sensitivity on the reader's domain data, if commodity GPU kernels lack efficient mixed-precision support (turning memory savings into latency regressions), or if the allocator's strategy does not transfer across models.
rationale: Mixed-precision quantization fits a single 24 GB GPU and can preserve quality better than uniform low-bit schemes, but the RL allocator overhead and kernel support requirements require workload-specific validation before production adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces uniform bit-width or heuristic-sensitivity weight quantization with layer-wise sensitivity measured by Fisher information and a reinforcement learning allocator that assigns per-layer bit-widths. Costs include a Fisher sensitivity estimation pass, training an RL allocator, and added deployment complexity from mixed-precision kernels, which may offset some memory savings relative to uniform low-bit formats. Can fail if Fisher estimates misrank sensitivity on the reader's domain data, if commodity GPU kernels lack efficient mixed-precision support (turning memory savings into latency regressions), or if the allocator's strategy does not transfer across models.

Outperforms 7 baselines with up to 3.39 lower perplexity, up to 6.87% higher accuracy, and up to 76% LLM-as-a-judge win rate across 7 models and 5 benchmarks; no multiplicative speed or memory factor is stated.
